title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: Clusters that are not purely superparamagnetic are described by a moment rigidly locked to the lattice, so the trajectory depends on initial rotational conditions; supersonic expansion cools rotation strongly while leaving vibration at the source temperature.
explanation: A locked moment precesses and nutates with the cluster rather than aligning freely with the field. Adiabatic entry makes the deflection distribution depend on rotational temperature and moment. A Tb23 fit gives about 2.81 μB per atom and a rotational temperature of 4 K, with an additional sharp undeflected component corresponding to roughly 10-20% superparamagnetic clusters.
scope: Locked-moment rare-earth clusters, illustrated for Tb23 and stated for the remaining non-superparamagnetic sizes; rotational cooling is a general feature of the supersonic beam.
conditions: Example profile at 98 K, B = 0.267 T, dB/dz = 101.3 T/m. Fit parameters are rotational temperature, magnetic moment, and superparamagnetic fraction.
caveats: The 4 K rotational temperature and 10-20% superparamagnetic fraction are fit results for the Tb23 profile, not universal constants. The model assumes adiabatic entry and a statistical distribution of initial conditions.
